Therefore excluded based on failure to meet task-based/emotion-regulation inclusion criteria.

EXCLUDE: Study uses structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) and behavioral correlations, not task-based fMRI, and does not report task-related brain activation. Inclusion met: I2 (emotion reappraisal task), I3 (healthy and patient groups reported). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using an emotional Stroop (eStroop) task assessing affective control (meets I1 and I2). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study where participants with GAD performed explicit emotion regulation (acceptance, worry, suppression) and the abstract reports task-related brain activations and connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I4. The abstract does not state whether a separate control group was included, so I3 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm sample/comparison details.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related connectivity/activation). Inclusion not met: I2 — study examines passive processing of emotional faces and genetic effects, not an emotion regulation instruction/strategy.

E2 met: study uses Theory-of-Mind/perspective-taking processing without instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (reports connectivity rather than explicit task-related activation results).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human adolescents during an emotion regulation task (including passive viewing of negative vs neutral visual stimuli) and reports task-related vmPFC–amygdala functional connectivity linked to psychopathology, matching the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Task-based fMRI where participants ignored task-irrelevant unpleasant words (emotional interference), representing cognitive control of emotion/emotion regulation; includes non-patient groups (high AP/AR/AD and controls) and reports task-related functional connectivity results. All inclusion criteria I1–I4 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract describes task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activations, but does not involve an emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (e.g., reappraisal/acceptance) nor explicit regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; therefore I2 not met. E2: Study examines perception/evaluation of others (active listening) without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instruction). Task-based fMRI in adolescents/young adults reporting rVLPFC activation to negative emotional words and links to emotion reappraisal and alcohol use. No evidence participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Abstract describes passive viewing and rating of aversive/neutral scenes; reports task fMRI activations (I1, I4) in clinical and control groups (I3). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study does not involve an emotion regulation task (I2 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: none of the exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion met: I3 (human clinical sample with separate controls). Inclusion NOT met: I1 (not task-based; resting-state fMRI), I2 (no emotion-regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation results reported). Therefore exclude.

Task-based fMRI in healthy humans; reports task-related activations. The emotional oddball requires distinguishing targets while ignoring negative vs neutral distractors, which involves cognitive control of emotional distraction (fits broad emotion-regulation or view-only inclusion). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where human participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate cravings (personal-food images), and reports task-related neural activation (frontoparietal network, multivariate analyses). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a resting-state fMRI study of emotional intelligence, not a task-based emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2 not applicable).

E2 met: study examined empathy for others' pain (participants observed needles inserted into body parts) without any instruction to amplify or dampen their emotional response; thus it is not an emotion regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of an instructed emotion regulation task).

Abstract does not report whether this is a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study or whether task-related activation contrasts meet inclusion criteria. Abstract reports human participants with social anxiety and neural/behavioral responses but does not specify that tasks were fMRI-based or involved explicit emotion regulation (or pure viewing), nor does it state task-related brain activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and healthy control groups), I4 (task-related connectivity results). Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (older adults) who performed an emotion-regulation task (increase/decrease responses to negative pictures, i.e., reappraisal/ regulation), and presents task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI using an emotion-word Stroop with emotional distractors; examines cognitive control of emotion in presence of affective stimuli and reports task-related brain activation in human adults. Meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI, emotion regulation/cognitive control, human participants, and reported activation results.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 — not an emotion-regulation task and stimuli are auditory (infant laughter), whereas the meta-analysis targets regulation or passive viewing of visual stimuli. No emotion-regulation instruction: the task was sex identification of auditory emotional vocalizations. Abstract provides insufficient information to determine whether this is a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. No task-based emotion-regulation paradigm is described. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Task-based fMRI study of implicit emotion processing (gender discrimination) in healthy human participants that reports task-related activation (amygdala BOLD response and functional connectivity) to emotional facial expressions. Task-based fMRI with human participants (OD/BPD and healthy controls) performing an oddball task requiring attention amid negative emotional distractors (interpretable as cognitive control of emotion/affective regulation), and reporting task-related activation differences. Task-based fMRI study in humans performing an explicit emotion regulation task (maintain/enhance/suppress) with patient (mTBI) and control groups and reporting task-related brain activation, meeting I1,I2,I3,I4; no exclusions met.

E2 met: study is a mentalizing/Prisoner's Dilemma fMRI task without instruction to amplify or dampen participants' own emotional responses. Abstract reports task-based fMRI in 9–19-year-olds and task-related amygdala activation (I1, I3, I4 met). This article is a review (Exclusion E1). Inclusion criteria met: none. This is a resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation; no task-related activation results are reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Abstract reports an emotional go/no-go task in adolescents addressing neural substrates of emotional reactivity and regulation, but it does not clearly state whether an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or fMRI activation results are reported. Excluded because the study does not meet I2: no emotion-regulation task was performed during fMRI (pressure-evoked pain used to assess CBT effects). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Study is an fMRI decision-making/ambiguity task, not an emotion regulation study. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Resting-state fMRI study without any task or emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants with control groups). Task-based fMRI with human participants viewing emotional (angry) faces and reporting task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 met). Task-based fMRI in humans reporting task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). No emotion-regulation task is described (I2 not met): abstract reports passive exposure to cues without instructions to regulate. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants with control group), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Task-based fMRI with adolescents performing an emotional attention task, reporting task-related brain activation.
